This is the most valuable issue in the tracker. If you have read the kit and thought "that would never
survive here", this is the template for saying so.

Be blunt. There is no need to soften it, no need to balance it with something positive, and no obligation
attached to sending it. A polite "interesting read" is the least useful possible response to this kit. A flat
"this falls apart the moment you have more than one inspector per shift, and here is why" is worth
considerably more. Nothing here is a product, so there is nothing to defend.

## Where does it break

The specific step, gate or assumption that does not hold. Be as concrete as you can — "gate 3 assumes there
is a second person available to approve, and on night shift there is not" beats "the approval stuff is
unrealistic".

## What does your process do differently

How the work actually happens where you are. The pattern is written from one view of how inspection and
non-conformance work, and that view is certainly too narrow somewhere. Volume, shift pattern, headcount,
who holds the tablet, whether the inspector is the operator, what the ERP already owns — any of it may be the
thing that breaks it.

## What would get routed around

If this were imposed where you work, what would people actually do instead? Keep a private spreadsheet and
enter it all on Friday? Leave records in `Draft` indefinitely? Share a login? Predicting the workaround is
often more useful than describing the flaw, because the workaround is the real failure mode.

## What would have to change

Your view of the fix, if you have one. "I do not know, but this is wrong" is a completely acceptable answer —
the observation is the contribution and you are not obliged to solve it.

## Anything about your context that helps

Rough size, sector, what platform you are on, whether you are certified to anything. Only what you are
comfortable sharing.

**Please keep employer material out of it.** Describe the shape of your process in general terms rather than
pasting procedures, forms, screenshots or real part, supplier or customer names.

---

One honest note: this is a personal project maintained in spare time by one person. Issues may go unanswered
for a long time, and some may never get a reply. That is a comment on this project's capacity, not on the
worth of what you sent — an objection that goes unanswered here is still worth making.
